questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Different culture, different ways of teaching and safety.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy and the international mobility team were very welcoming.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received an introduction to the international mobility program and were told where to find the team.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is one residence on campus, which I lived in.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were different stores and restaurants on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The housing on campus is quite expensive, but has a nice location and is convenient. Most student live in Lisbon in stead though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We just registered on the welcome day when we arrived.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international mobility team as well as other employees who could help with different things introduced themselves on the welcome day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the bidding process is quite complex, so you need to spend some time to watch videos about how it works, which the school gives you a link to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses had a quite low level compared to courses at my home university, whereas other courses had a too high level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was much more group work and evaluations throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International migration, Introduction to machine learning, Environmental policy, Impact investment, Economics of health and health care, Economics of education, Financial crises in history, Entrepreneurship

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I especially liked the courses international migration, economics of education and financial crises in history. I feel like all courses were very relevant from an economist's perspective and I got a lot of new insights from these courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were no unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices were as I expected or even lower.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were sunset bars, pizza quizzes, parties, sports clubs and plenty other activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sunset bars and the parties as well as the activities in the introduction week were very fun. Furthermore, there were great opportunities for surfing and parties in the surf club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Other students should definitely visit Porto, Algarve, Nazare and Sintra on their weekends. Furthermore, Madeira is supposed to be really nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Portuguese were very welcoming and including.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to other students in class and participate in social activities, also through Erasmus Lisboa.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the processes at the university were a bit unorganized and I did not always get clear information about courses and exams.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Portuguese were very open and kind people, which I appreciated.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the 7 ECTS courses are in general much tougher than the 3,5 ECTS courses, you cannot expect good weather all the time and Portuguese people are a minority at the university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can come up with right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of different people and being induced to participate actively in class and speak in front of the class, as well as working together in groups with people from many different cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In some periods, the workload was very high, especially because we had to do 31,5 ECTS.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
